title: Baselines and fair comparisons
outcome: Explain baselines and fair comparisons using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: A baseline deserves a fair chance. Two classifiers answer the same eight fixed questions with the same allowed sources.
given: Simple rule A: 6/8 correct. New model B: 7/8 correct. No test case is used to tune either version.

steps.label: Declare baseline
steps.detail: A uses a simple documented rule rather than an intentionally weak placeholder.

steps.label: Measure fairly
steps.detail: A is 75%; B is 87.5% on the same eight cases.

steps.label: Interpret cautiously
steps.detail: B adds one correct case here; compare resources and failure types too.

explanation: A baseline anchors the claim of improvement. Fair comparison keeps information access, cases and scoring aligned while allowing the declared method difference.

counterfactual.change: Give B the answer key before testing.
counterfactual.prediction: The resulting comparison is invalid as unseen evaluation.
counterfactual.reason: B would receive privileged information that A did not receive.

student_task: Calculate 6/8 and 7/8 correctness and name the one-case gain. Why is giving B the answer key incompatible with an unseen comparison to the simple baseline?
teacher_answer: A uses a simple documented rule rather than an intentionally weak placeholder. A is 75%; B is 87.5% on the same eight cases. B adds one correct case here; compare resources and failure types too. Changed case: The resulting comparison is invalid as unseen evaluation. B would receive privileged information that A did not receive.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Eight cases do not establish a stable advantage or statistical significance.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
